en: The Questions of King Milinda:
The Introduction to the Book of Puzzles;
The Chapter on the Qualities of a Lay Disciple.
3. The Nine Who Destroy Secrets and Mantras “Venerable Nāgasena, there are these nine persons who disclose secrets that have been entrusted to them and do not keep them.
Which are the nine?”
“One who is dominated by passion, one dominated by hatred, one dominated by delusion, one who is timid, one who is heavy with worldly gain, one addicted to women,
a eunuch, and a child. The Elder asked, “What is their fault?”
“Venerable Nāgasena, one of lustful temperament reveals and does not keep secret what was deliberated in confidence due to lust;

one of hateful temperament reveals and does not keep secret what was deliberated in confidence due to hatred; one who is deluded reveals and does not keep secret what was deliberated in confidence due to delusion;
one who is fearful reveals and does not keep secret what was deliberated in confidence due to fear.”

One who is heavy with worldly gain reveals secrets whispered for the sake of gain and does not keep them; a woman reveals secrets whispered due to the shallowness of her wisdom and does not keep them;
a drunkard reveals secrets whispered due to his addiction to liquor and does not keep them;
a eunuch reveals secrets whispered due to his indecisiveness and does not keep them; a child [reveals secrets] due to his fickleness...
He reveals what was spoken in secret and does not keep it hidden.
It is said here:
"One who is lustful, hateful, and deluded..."
One who is timid, one heavy with worldly desires,
a woman, a drunkard, and a eunuch—
the ninth is a male child.
These nine persons in the world are short-lived,
wavering, and fickle;
what is kept secret by them is revealed.
"Quickly it becomes manifest.
These are the nine types of persons who destroy secret counsel.
